summary: The single HTML page of the dashboard. It is served at `/` by `dashboard()` in `iip/app.py`, which first swaps the API-key placeholder, and it holds only the static shell: the navigation rail, the top bar, the `#view` outlet that `main.js` renders pages into, and empty hosts for the boot overlay, drawer, palette and toasts. Because the shell is plain HTML, the navigation and chrome are drawn before any script runs; JavaScript (one ES module plus the vendored anime.js) fills in everything else.

notes.text: Declares HTML5, so the browser renders in standards mode rather than legacy quirks mode.

The root element. `lang="en"` tells screen readers and the browser the page language. `data-motion` is the in-app motion switch: `motion.js` flips it to `off` at startup if the user saved that preference, `motionEnabled()` reads it, and `base.css` disables CSS transitions and keyframe animations while it is `off`.
Opens the document head: metadata, styles and scripts, nothing visible.
Declares UTF-8, so characters used across the UI such as `·`, `…` and `⌘` display correctly.
Makes phones lay the page out at the device's width instead of a zoomed-out desktop view; `layout.css` turns the rail into a bottom bar below 860px.
Default tab title. `route()` in `main.js` replaces it on every navigation, e.g. 'Events · IIP'.
Short page description used by search engines and link previews.

**Demo-mode API key injection.** When the server renders `/` it replaces the `__IIP_API_KEY__` placeholder with the real key if demo mode is on, or with an empty string if not; `api.js` reads this tag and sends the key as `X-API-Key` on write requests. It is a demo convenience only: anyone who views the page source can see the key.
Colours the mobile browser's address bar with `#0a0b0d`, the same value as the `--bg` token in `tokens.css`, so the browser chrome blends into the dark UI.
The tab icon, an SVG served from the `/static` mount (the backend also answers `/favicon.ico` with the same file).

`preconnect` hints let the browser open connections to Google Fonts' two hosts early, before the stylesheet asks for them. `crossorigin` is needed for `fonts.gstatic.com` because font files are fetched in CORS mode, so the warmed-up connection must be a CORS one too.

Loads the three typefaces the design tokens refer to: Geist for UI text (weights 400 to 700), Geist Mono for numbers, IDs and labels, and Instrument Serif in regular and italic for headings. `display=swap` shows a fallback font immediately and swaps the web font in when it arrives, so text is never invisible.

The foundation stylesheets, in cascade order: `tokens.css` defines the design variables (colours such as `--bg`, fonts, radii), `base.css` holds the reset, the backdrop and the reduced-motion rules, and `layout.css` positions the shell, rail, top bar and boot screen. There is no build step, so these are served exactly as written in `web/css`.

The more specific layers come last so they can build on the ones above: reusable components (panels, buttons, the switch, drawer, palette and toasts), chart styles, and per-page styles (including the top progress bar).
Comment: anime.js v4 is MIT-licensed and **vendored** (copied into `web/vendor`) instead of loaded from a CDN, so the demo also works offline. Its UMD build attaches itself to `window.anime`.

Loads anime.js with `defer`: it downloads in parallel with parsing and runs after the document has been parsed, in document order, so it is ready before `main.js` runs. If the file fails to load, `motion.js` notices that `window.anime` is missing and simply skips motion.

The app's entry point, loaded as a native **ES module**: the browser follows its `import` statements itself, which is why the frontend needs no bundler. Module scripts are deferred automatically, so it runs after the DOM is parsed and after the deferred anime.js script above.
Closes the head.
Opens the body; everything visible lives inside it.
A purely decorative layer: `base.css` draws a fixed dot grid and a soft accent glow behind the app. `aria-hidden="true"` keeps it out of the accessibility tree.

The thin progress bar at the very top of the window. CSS starts its inner `i` element at `scaleX(0)`, and `route()` in `main.js` animates it during each navigation; it is decorative, hence `aria-hidden`.

Container for the first-visit **boot sequence**. It starts with the `hidden` attribute: `boot.js` reveals it only on the first visit of a browser session with motion enabled and otherwise removes it, so a failed script can never leave a cover over the app.
Inner column (`.boot-inner` in `layout.css`); the overlay's grid centres it on screen, and its contents line up on the left.
Row holding the logo mark and the product name.
Inline SVG version of the logo on a 32 by 32 grid. `fill="none"` is the default because the traces are drawn as strokes (CSS gives the core circle its fill), and `aria-hidden` marks it as decorative.
The two `.trace` paths that form the logo's connector shape (a bracket and a short bar). `boot.js` passes them to `drawIn()`, which animates their strokes so the logo appears to draw itself.
The `.core` circle, the accent dot; `boot.js` pops it in by scaling it from 0 to 1 with an overshooting `outBack` ease.
Closes the SVG.
The product name in the serif typeface, with the `em` part in italics; `boot.js` fades and slides it in.
Closes the logo row.
Empty on purpose: `boot.js` appends status lines here built from real numbers fetched from the API (how many signals and levels the rulebook has, how many events are stored).
The boot progress bar; `boot.js` scales its inner `i` element one step further for each status line.
Hint text: `boot.js` listens for any key press, or a click on the overlay, and then skips the remaining lines.
Close `.boot-inner` and the `#boot` overlay.
The app shell: `layout.css` makes it a two-column grid, with the navigation rail on the left and the main column on the right.
The left rail, an `aside` because it is secondary to the main content. It stays in place while the page scrolls (`position: sticky`) and becomes a bottom bar on narrow screens.
The brand block doubles as a home link to `#/overview`; `aria-label` gives it a concise accessible name ('IIP home') instead of the logo text.
The logo mark at rail size, again decorative (`aria-hidden`).
A rounded square tile behind the mark, with its fill and hairline border written directly as SVG attributes.
The same two connector traces and accent core as the boot logo, with slightly thicker strokes; `layout.css` colours `.trace` grey and `.core` with the accent colour.
Closes the SVG.
Brand name with a small monospaced subtitle; on narrow screens CSS hides the whole brand block.
Closes the brand link.
The main navigation landmark; `aria-label="Main"` names it for screen-reader users.

The **sliding highlight** behind the active link. It is absolutely positioned at the top of the nav, and `moveIndicator()` in `main.js` moves it down by the active link's `offsetTop` (spring-animated, or instantly on first load).
Group label 'Monitor'; `eyebrow` is the small uppercase monospaced label style from `base.css`.

Overview link. The `href` is a hash URL, so clicking only changes `location.hash` and the router in `main.js` renders the page without a reload; `data-page` lets `route()` find and mark the active link. The inline Lucide-style icon uses `stroke="currentColor"` so it follows the link's text colour, and the `.kbd` badge shows the keyboard shortcut (g then o) on hover.
Events link with the 'activity' pulse icon; shortcut g then e. Like all nav icons it is inlined in the HTML rather than generated by `icons.js`, so the rail is fully drawn before any JavaScript runs.

Incidents link with the shield icon. Instead of a shortcut hint it carries the `#open-count` badge, hidden until `refreshCounts()` in `main.js` finds open incidents (new live incidents then bump it). The g then i shortcut still works because it is defined in `pages/index.js`.
Customers link. Its route is `#/users` (the page module is `users.js`) and its shortcut is g then c.
Group label 'Engine' for the risk-engine pages.
Risk Lab link (flask icon), the page where you toggle signals and watch the real engine score them; shortcut g then l.
Simulation link (lightning icon), where attack scenarios are replayed through the real pipeline; shortcut g then s.
Group label 'Platform'.
Integration link (plug icon): connection health, metrics and a live API console. Its shortcut is g then n, because i is taken by Incidents.
AI Analyst link (sparkles icon), the chat page that explains incidents and scores; shortcut g then a.
Closes the nav.
The rail footer; `margin-top: auto` in `layout.css` pushes it to the bottom of the rail.
First status card: the live connection.

The connection indicator. `#live-dot` starts with the `warn` class (a yellow pulse) and `#live-label` reads 'Connecting'; `renderLiveState()` in `main.js` updates both whenever `live.js` reports a new state on the bus. The few inline styles are one-off layout tweaks.
An 'SSE' tag naming the transport (Server-Sent Events); then the row closes.
Closes the connection card.
Second card: the demo traffic generator.
The label 'Live traffic' with a small 'demo generator' caption beneath it.

The toggle. `role="switch"` plus `aria-checked` makes screen readers announce it as an on/off switch, and CSS styles the knob from that same attribute; `wireTraffic()` in `main.js` sets its starting value, handles clicks and keeps it in sync with the server. Then the row closes.
Close the traffic card, the rail footer and the rail.
The main column: top bar plus the page outlet.
The top bar; `layout.css` makes it sticky so it stays visible while the page scrolls.
Breadcrumbs 'NovaBank / page'; `route()` writes the current page's title into `#crumb`.
An empty, flexible spacer that pushes the search button and the clock to the right edge.
Button that opens the **command palette**; `main.js` attaches its click handler. `aria-label` names it explicitly because the visible label is hidden on small screens.
Magnifying-glass icon, drawn inline.
The visible label and the shortcut hint 'Ctrl K'; `main.js` rewrites the hint to '⌘ K' on Apple devices.
Closes the button.
UTC clock, filled in and updated every second by `startClock()` in `main.js`; `aria-label` explains what the numbers are.
Closes the top bar.

The **router outlet**. `route()` in `main.js` empties it and each page module's `render()` mounts its content here. `tabindex="-1"` makes the region focusable from script without adding it to the Tab order.
Close the main column and the shell.
Host for the right-hand detail drawer, hidden until `drawer.js` mounts a sheet into it.
Host for the command palette, hidden until `palette.js` mounts it (Ctrl/⌘+K).
Stack for toast notifications. `aria-live="polite"` makes screen readers announce new toasts when they finish what they are reading, without interrupting.
Shown only when JavaScript is disabled: the dashboard cannot work without it, but the API's interactive documentation at `/docs` still does.
Close the body and the document.
